question: A certain sum becomes double in 2 years at a certain rate per annum compound interest. The number of years it will become 4 times at the same compound interest rate is:
solution:
Given:

A certain sum becomes double in 2 years at a certain rate per annum compound interest.

Concept used:

In case of the compound interest,

Amount = P(1 + R/100)N

CI = P(1 + R/100)N - P

Where, P = Principal, R = Rate of Interest, N = Time in years

Calculation:

Let the rate of interest and principal be R% and P respectively

According to the question,

P(1 + R/100)² = 2P

⇒ (1 + R/100)2 = 2

⇒ (1 + R/100)4 = 2² (Squaring both sides)

⇒ P(1 + R/100)4 = 22 × P (Multiplying P on both sides)

⇒ P(1 + R/100)4 = 4 × P ....(1)

Now, from (1), we can clearly conclude in 4 years the principal will become 4 times in amount at the same rate of interest.

**∴ The number of years it will become 4 times at the same compound interest rate is 4 years.**
